# Disposable ephemeral deletion fixture

Run `python3 packages/tests/fixtures/ephemeral-deletion-convex/run.py` only with ports 3540 and 3541 free. It starts a fresh loopback database, disables beacon and telemetry before synchronization, strips inherited provider variables, and stops only its own backend. It deploys the actual product schema and re-exports the registered product cleanup and guarded telemetry claim mutations; the public fixture bridge seeds synthetic data and invokes those mutations. Synthetic transaction cases supply user IDs directly. A separate case signs up and signs in using the installed auth .8 username/password components; its test-only bridge derives the user ID from the real session before calling the product claim and cleanup mutations. No provider or external service is contacted.

The test covers over 100 rows per table, concurrent calls, replay, request matching, transactional rollback, other-owner and anonymous identity retention, the global issuance bucket, billing attempts, compute debits, webhook deliveries, receipts, and the user record. A synthetic changed-request test checks progress cannot carry over to a different request. It does not delete financial records or prove whole-account erasure. With the product telemetry fence integrated, it also checks concurrent pending-owner claims, anonymous attachment denial, and post-completion claim denial without changing the issuance bucket. It cannot attribute anonymous identities or prove telemetry delivery. The production telemetry HTTP route remains disabled by the E2E gate and is not exercised.
